questions.question: Imagine a triangle cut from paper. Its three sides measure 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm. What is this triangle called when we sort it by its sides?
options: Equilateral, because all three sides are the same length
Isosceles, because exactly two sides are the same length
Scalene, because all three sides are used to make it
It has no side name, because all three sides are equal
questions.explain: Sorting by sides means counting how many side lengths match: three equal sides means equilateral. The common trap is stopping at 'two sides match, so isosceles' — check all three before naming it.

questions.question: Imagine a triangle cut from paper. Its three sides measure 8 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm. What is this triangle called when we sort it by its sides?
options: Scalene, because the three sides are not all the same length
Isosceles, because exactly two sides are the same length
Equilateral, because two of the sides match
It has no side name, because only two of the three sides match
questions.explain: Two matching sides and one different side make an isosceles triangle. The trap is thinking scalene means 'not equilateral' — scalene means every side is a different length, and here two sides are both 8 cm.

questions.question: Imagine a triangle cut from paper. Its three sides measure 4 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm. What is this triangle called when we sort it by its sides?
options: Isosceles, because no two sides are equal
Equilateral, because it has three sides
Scalene, because all three sides have different lengths
It cannot be sorted by its sides at all
questions.explain: When no two sides match, the triangle is scalene. A common mix-up is thinking equilateral means 'three sides' — every triangle has three sides; equilateral means three EQUAL sides.

questions.question: Which sentence describes a scalene triangle?
options: Exactly two of its sides have the same length
It is a polygon made of three straight sides
All three of its sides have the same length
All three of its sides have different lengths
questions.explain: Scalene means no sides match at all — all three lengths are different. The trap is confusing it with equilateral (all three equal) or with the plain definition of a triangle, which is true of every triangle.

questions.question: A triangle has two sides that each measure 7 cm, and its perimeter is 20 cm. How should it be sorted by its sides?
options: Isosceles, because the third side is 6 cm, so exactly two sides match
Equilateral, because the third side must also be 7 cm
Scalene, because the third side is 6 cm, so all three sides are different
You cannot tell without knowing the three angles
questions.explain: Find the missing side first: 20 − 7 − 7 = 6 cm, so the sides are 7 cm, 7 cm and 6 cm — two match, so isosceles. The trap is calling it scalene because one side is different; scalene needs ALL three to be different.

questions.question: Maya cuts a triangle from cardboard for an art project. Its perimeter is 21 cm and all three sides are the same length. Which statement is true?
options: It is equilateral and each side is 63 cm
It is equilateral and each side is 7 cm
It is equilateral and each side is 3 cm
There is not enough information to find the side lengths
questions.explain: Equal sides means you share the perimeter equally: 21 ÷ 3 = 7 cm each. The usual slips are multiplying by 3 instead of dividing, or dividing by the wrong number — always divide the perimeter by 3.

questions.question: Which set of side lengths makes a scalene triangle?
options: 4 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm
6 cm, 6 cm, 6 cm
3 cm, 5 cm, 7 cm
5 cm, 8 cm, 5 cm
questions.explain: For scalene, compare every pair of sides — all three must be different, as in 3 cm, 5 cm and 7 cm. Watch the set with 5 cm, 8 cm, 5 cm: the matching sides are not written side by side, but they still match, so that one is isosceles.

questions.question: The three side lengths of a triangular sail are 8 cm, 8 cm and 11 cm on a scale drawing. Which statement about these three numbers and the triangle is correct?
options: The mode is 11 cm, so the triangle is isosceles
There is no mode, so the triangle is scalene
The mode is 9 cm, and the triangle is scalene
The mode is 8 cm, and the triangle is isosceles
questions.explain: The mode is the length that repeats, 8 cm, and a repeated side length is exactly what makes a triangle isosceles. The trap is giving 9 cm — that is the mean, since (8 + 8 + 11) ÷ 3 = 9, not the mode.

questions.question: Emma looks at a triangle with sides of 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm and says, ‘This one cannot be called isosceles, because isosceles triangles have two equal sides and this triangle has three.’ Which response is best?
options: Emma is not quite right — the triangle does have at least two equal sides, so it fits isosceles too, but equilateral is the more exact name
Emma is right — for isosceles, the third side has to be a different length from the other two
Emma is right — a triangle can have only one side name, so equilateral rules out isosceles
Emma is not quite right — the triangle is really scalene, because all three of its sides are counted
questions.explain: Isosceles means at least two sides are equal, so a triangle with three equal sides fits that description as well — equilateral is just the more precise name for it. The common misconception is thinking the side names never overlap.

questions.question: Noah builds a triangular kite frame in his Surrey backyard using three sticks: 45 cm, 45 cm and 30 cm. The 30 cm stick snaps, so he replaces it with another 45 cm stick. How does the way we sort his frame by its sides change?
options: It changes from scalene to isosceles
It changes from isosceles to equilateral
It changes from isosceles to scalene
It stays isosceles, because two sticks were already equal
questions.explain: Before the swap two sides matched (45, 45, 30), so it was isosceles; afterwards all three are 45 cm, so it becomes equilateral. The trap is calling the first frame scalene — scalene needs all three sides different, and two were already 45 cm.

questions.question: Priya measures a triangular floor tile and finds the sides are 12 cm, 12 cm and 12 cm. She writes: ‘Scalene, because all three sides are the same.’ What is her mistake?
options: Nothing is wrong — scalene does mean all three sides are the same
She should have written isosceles, because only two sides are allowed to match
She swapped the meanings: scalene means all three sides are DIFFERENT, so this tile is equilateral
She should have measured the angles first, because the side names come from angles
questions.explain: Her measuring was fine; she used the wrong name — scalene means every side is a different length, and three equal sides means equilateral. Keep the meanings apart: equilateral = all equal, isosceles = at least two equal, scalene = none equal.

questions.question: At a Kelowna community garden, a triangular plant marker is described like this: the shortest side is 6 cm, the second side is 2 cm longer than the shortest side, and the third side is 3 cm longer than the second side. How is this marker sorted by its sides?
options: Isosceles — two of the sides are built from the same starting side, so they must match
Scalene — the sides are 6 cm, 2 cm and 3 cm
Scalene — the sides are 6 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm
Scalene — the sides are 6 cm, 8 cm and 11 cm, and all three are different
questions.explain: Work out each side before naming the triangle: 6 cm, then 6 + 2 = 8 cm, then 8 + 3 = 11 cm — three different lengths, so scalene. The common slips are adding the 3 cm to the shortest side instead of the second side, or writing the 2 cm and 3 cm differences as if they were the side lengths themselves.
